answer.rationale: Finance mandate requires 18% component spend reduction; incumbent has refused to reopen price. Low-cost vendor's quote already meets the mandate on its own. Memory c2 (verified) records that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply last year with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, which directly supports a primary switch here. Memory c6 (multi-year incumbent volume pricing) is acknowledged but does not apply because the incumbent will not reopen price this cycle, so the volume-pricing lever is unavailable. Renewal/stability benefits from c1 are outweighed by the hard cost mandate the low-cost vendor already satisfies. Delivery risk is the residual concern with the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, but the low-cost vendor's prior onboarding was quick and invoicing accurate, and switching primary supply now (rather than dual-sourcing or deferring) is the single decision that delivers the mandate within one cycle. Deferring (c5) preserves flexibility but does not achieve the 18% cut; adding a second source (c3) spreads volume and would dilute the cost gain needed to meet the mandate. Single switch primary vendor is the minimal-risk, mandate-meeting action.
